verdict.rationale: NVIDIA documents a second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine on this part that accelerates LLM inference across PyTorch and TensorFlow. A hands-on four-card build reports reaching 41k tok/s, but a community critic notes that SM120 lacks support in the main libraries, which target SM100/B300. missing for 10: documented FP4 support, named serving-stack support for TensorRT-LLM, vLLM or llama.cpp on this part, and independent confirmation that the major inference libraries are optimized for SM120.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, this GPU has a documented LLM inference story — low-precision formats (FP8/FP4) and supported serving stacks (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, ROCm, llama.cpp) for this part

citations.quote: A second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine—shared with data center-class NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs—accelerates LLM prototyping, inference, and AI development across frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch.
After the fix they got back to 41k tok/s.
